reason: Conversation 2 obtained the model number and steered the homeowner to the sensible low-cost test (a switched-off full manual defrost) with practical safety and food-handling guidance, matching the expected first step for a post-power-cut warm fridge. Its weakness is asserting a fan-and-vent architecture that doesn't fit this static-cooled Hotpoint and stating the ice-blockage theory too confidently. Conversation 1 never suggested a defrost, repeatedly failed to track the customer's answers (thanking them for 'fan noise' and 'coils' they never reported, then declaring 'blocked vents' most likely after they said there were none) and jumped straight to a refrigeration engineer; it was honest about uncertainty and recommended no parts, but neither conversation mentioned routing the fault through the landlord/letting agent.
